mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility acts as a leading indicator of daytime foot traffic near commercial corridors; sustained levels of WORKPLACES mobility propagate directly into RETAIL_REC through commuter-adjacent shopping and lunch-hour errands over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC moves opposite to the 4-week trend direction of WORKPLACES in more than half of observed weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility above 10 points indicates heightened household risk-aversion or confinement behavior, which suppresses discretionary outings and pulls RETAIL_REC down over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 10 points in a weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline in the two weeks following any week where RESIDENTIAL exceeds 10 points.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous sharp drops in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signal an active policy tightening regime (e.g., restricted movement or closures) that mechanically depresses retail visits within the same week due to reduced commuting-linked shopping opportunities.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall more than 10 points week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -23.4 to -43.3 between t-2w and t-1w while TRANSIT fell from -23.6 to -33.3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following a joint sharp decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility declines sharply while TRANSIT also declines, the joint pattern indicates an active stay-at-home dynamic rather than isolated weather effects, compounding to suppress RETAIL_REC more than either series alone would predict, over the next month.

evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -36.9 and TRANSIT worsened to -21.0 at t-0w after a one-week rebound
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the following four weeks despite simultaneous sharp drops in PARKS and TRANSIT in more than half of observed instances.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility reflects outdoor-activity substitution; when PARKS trends downward independent of policy shocks, suppressed outdoor options shift some discretionary activity back toward indoor retail and recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC modestly over the following month.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -14.6 to -36.9 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines alongside a sustained decline in PARKS over four consecutive weeks.

failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the following two weeks despite concurrent RESIDENTIAL increase and flat GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in TRANSIT mobility of more than 10 points after a prior sharp decline signals restored commuting and transit-linked foot traffic, which feeds through to increased RETAIL_REC within the following two weeks via renewed urban-core visits.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 10 points week-on-week after a prior weekly decline
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -33.3 at t-1w to -21.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks following a greater-than-10-point rebound in TRANSIT.
